1. Core Clinical Tension: A 42-year-old male presents with chronic wasting, low-grade fevers, pancytopenia, marked hypergammaglobulinemia, and extensive peripheral and mesenteric lymphadenopathy. In the Indian subcontinent, visceral leishmaniasis classically manifests with massive splenomegaly without prominent peripheral adenopathy; this unusual prominent lymphadenopathy led to empiric anti-tubercular therapy and mimicked disseminated tuberculosis or lymphoma.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission presentation concludes after the 1-year history of fever and weight loss, physical exam demonstrating lymphadenopathy and mild hepatosplenomegaly, abdominal ultrasound showing conglomerate mesenteric lymph nodes, baseline complete hemogram (pancytopenia), and clinical chemistry (severe A:G reversal), stopping strictly prior to fine-needle aspiration cytology, bone marrow examination, and rK39 serology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Disseminated tuberculosis causes chronic fever, wasting, pancytopenia, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy in endemic settings but was excluded by negative acid-fast stains, mycobacterial culture, and PCR; lymphoma or plasma cell dyscrasia presents with adenopathy, pancytopenia, and rouleaux but cytology and bone marrow aspirate demonstrated intracellular amastigotes within histiocytes.
case_prompt: A 42-year-old male presented to the medical emergency department with complaints of weakness and significant weight loss over 1 year. He had experienced recurrent episodes of low-grade fever over the preceding year, for which he had been treated for chronic cavitary granulomatous pulmonary infection 2 years previously. He had recently completed 1 month of empiric antitubercular therapy without clinical improvement. There was no significant family history. On physical examination, the patient was thin, pale, and afebrile with abdominal distension. Left submandibular and left axillary lymph nodes were enlarged, each measuring 1.5 cm in diameter. Abdominal examination revealed mild hepatosplenomegaly without a fluid thrill. Abdominal ultrasound revealed multiple enlarged conglomerate mesenteric lymph nodes, with the largest measuring 22 mm x 18 mm. Complete hemogram showed pancytopenia: hemoglobin 6.0 g/dL, total leukocyte count 1,800/mcL (47% polymorphonuclear cells, 51% lymphocytes, 1% eosinophils, 1% monocytes), platelet count 48,000/mcL, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 50 mm/h. Peripheral blood smear showed rouleaux formation without hemoparasites. Serum chemistry revealed an albumin-to-globulin reversal: total protein 9.5 g/dL, albumin 2.0 g/dL, globulin 7.5 g/dL, and an A:G ratio of 1:3.75. Renal and liver function tests were otherwise normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: High initial suspicion given previous pulmonary tuberculosis, chronic low-grade fever, weight loss, generalized and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and failure to improve on empiric antitubercular therapy; definitively excluded by negative Ziehl-Neelsen staining, negative PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and negative mycobacterial culture.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: In view of strong clinical suspicion, Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) was also done which came out to be negative. Both polymerase chain reaction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and AFB culture yielded negative result.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Hematologic Malignancy / Lymphoma or Plasma Cell Dyscrasia
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to generalized and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and severe hypergammaglobulinemia with peripheral smear rouleaux; ruled out by lymph node cytology and bone marrow examination showing reactive plasmacytosis without clonal neoplastic proliferation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Clinical chemistry revealed A:G reversal with total protein of 9.5 g%, albumin of 2.0 g%, globulin of 7.5 g%, and A:G ratio of 1:3.75.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point was fine-needle aspiration cytology of the enlarged lymph nodes revealing epithelioid granulomas and numerous intracellular and extracellular amastigote forms, corroborated by positive rK39 antigen and bone marrow aspirate confirming visceral leishmaniasis complicated by underlying advanced HIV infection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Smears prepared showed few epithelioid cell granulomas interspersed with discrete and aggregates of histiocytes in a background of reactive lymphoid cells and many plasma cells. Numerous intracellular as well as extracellular amastigote forms of Leishmania species were seen

editor_comments: Distilled strictly to emergency admission triage. Unusual Indian visceral leishmaniasis presenting with extensive peripheral and mesenteric adenopathy, pancytopenia, and A:G reversal; confirmed by lymph node FNAC and rK39.
